title: Heart Attack (Chest Pain)
summary: Call immediately for chest pain that could be a heart attack. Keep them resting and, if appropriate, give aspirin to chew. Be ready for CPR.

callEmergency.headline: Call {EMERGENCY} now for possible heart attack
when: Chest pain, pressure or tightness lasting more than a few minutes or coming and going
Pain spreading to the arm, neck, jaw, back or stomach
Chest discomfort with breathlessness, sweating, nausea or light-headedness
Women, older adults and people with diabetes may have less typical symptoms – call if in doubt

steps.title: Call {EMERGENCY}
steps.text: Do not let them drive themselves. Send for an AED.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Help them into a comfortable position – often sitting, leaning against a support with knees bent. Loosen tight clothing and reassure them.

steps.title: Aspirin
steps.text: If they are an adult, conscious, able to swallow and not allergic to aspirin, and have not been told not to take it, give aspirin to chew.
points: AHA: 1 adult (325 mg) or 2–4 low-dose (81 mg) tablets
steps.caution: Do not give aspirin for chest pain caused by injury, or if they are allergic, have a bleeding disorder or have been told not to take it.

steps.title: Their own medication
steps.text: If they have prescribed angina medication (e.g. nitroglycerin/GTN spray), help them take it as directed.

steps.title: Monitor
steps.text: Stay with them and watch breathing. If they become unresponsive and stop breathing normally, start CPR and use an AED.

doNot: Do not let them walk around or exert themselves
Do not give aspirin to children or teenagers, or for chest pain after an injury
Do not delay calling to see if the pain passes
